candidates.core_provocation: While preparing a class video for graduation, a student finds footage of a classmate whom nobody—including the teacher—remembers. The student must discover why the school has erased this person from its records before the video is shown to everyone.
candidates.why_interesting: A familiar school memory becomes a mystery, with the exciting question of whether the forgotten student was a victim, a danger, or someone the protagonist betrayed.

candidates.core_provocation: A teacher asks students to write about the most important event of the school year, but every student remembers the same ordinary day differently—and one version reveals a secret the school has worked hard to hide.
candidates.why_interesting: The tension comes from knowing that memory may be wrong while still holding the key to a real crime or betrayal.

candidates.core_provocation: A student secretly records classmates’ memories because they are afraid of forgetting, then discovers a new recording describing an event that has not happened yet. The recording also contains the voice of a classmate who disappeared from school months ago.
candidates.why_interesting: The story combines a personal fear of forgetting with a concrete, urgent mystery about whether the future—or the past—is being changed.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The forgotten classmate creates an immediate visual mystery and keeps the action focused on one school project, a small group of characters, and a clear deadline. It also allows the secret to become emotionally powerful: the protagonist may have to choose between protecting the school’s version of the past and telling the truth.
